I have farmed this land in Quzhou for 45 years. I am 59 now, and I know every mu of my 10.7 mu plot. My household has four people, but some of the younger ones work off-farm in the city, so I must manage the labor carefully. We have a well for irrigation, but water is precious and pumping costs money, so I do not waste it.

For wheat, I will plant the full 10.7 mu after the maize harvest in October. I will use rotary tillage to prepare the seedbed, then sow an improved variety like the ones I buy from the supply shop. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and topdress with urea at the jointing stage in spring. I irrigate three times: once before winter to help the crop survive the cold, once at jointing, and once at heading. I spray pesticides three times—herbicide early, then insecticide and fungicide when I see problems. A good wheat crop should give me around 500 kg per mu.

For maize, I plant the same 10.7 mu right after harvesting the wheat in early June. Time is short, so I do not till the soil; I seed directly into the wheat stubble using no-tillage. I plant hybrid seed because it grows fast and strong. I apply fertilizer at sowing and again at the big trumpet stage. I irrigate twice, usually at jointing and filling, because summer rain sometimes helps. I spray twice for weeds and insects. With good weather, I expect about 600 kg per mu from the maize.
